subject.title: [security] SSH host key verification is disabled for Namespace Instance, Phala, and Islo SSH targets

question: What host identity model should Namespace Instance, Phala, and Islo use before Crabbox sends SSH workflow data over these provider proxy paths?
rationale: The source-reproducible issue crosses Crabbox's documented SSH trust boundary, but the durable fix may affect provider compatibility and must choose between host-key pinning, provider-supplied identity, existing gateway TLS, or an explicit insecure opt-in.

options.title: Verify host identity by default
options.body: Remove the unconditional bypass and implement per-lease or provider-scoped host-key verification for all three adapters with focused regression coverage.

options.title: Use provider-specific trust roots
options.body: Accept a documented provider identity mechanism such as Phala's verified TLS gateway only where maintainers consider it equivalent, and fix the remaining adapters separately.

options.title: Gate insecure compatibility
options.body: Keep current connectivity only behind an explicit trusted opt-in and warning for providers that cannot yet provide stable server identity.

recommendation.title: Verify host identity by default
recommendation.body: Remove the unconditional bypass and implement per-lease or provider-scoped host-key verification for all three adapters with focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the strongest routing point from current SSH builder blame, Namespace provider history, and adjacent security-boundary work.
